title: USWNT legend Becky Sauerbrunn returns to Portland as technical consultant
content:
USWNT and Portland Thorns legend Becky Sauerbrunn is coming back to the Rose City to assist the club as a technical consultant for the remainder of the 2026 season.

A two-time Women’s World Cup winner, three-time NWSL champion and four-time NWSL defender of the year, Sauerbrunn aims to bring her expertise and mentorship to the players.

“My role will be multifaceted,” Sauerbrunn told The Athletic. “I’ll work with the back line, but I’ll also be a resource for the coaching staff and the players. I’ve been in this league a long time, so I can offer context on different teams, players and identities.”

Sauerbrunn was one of the NWSL’s original players, joining FC Kansas City for the league’s inaugural season in 2013. Over 12 seasons and 189 appearances, she became one of the league’s most decorated defenders.

After five seasons with Kansas City and two with the Utah Royals, Sauerbrunn joined Portland in 2020. She made 72 regular season appearances for the Thorns, helping the club win the 2022 NWSL Championship, the 2021 Shield and Challenge Cup, among other trophies, before retiring after the 2024 season.

“There’s also a leadership component. The Thorns have lost a lot of veteran voices in recent years with Christine Sinclair and Megan Klingenberg retiring, and my own retirement,” Sauerbrunn said. “A team environment is a delicate ecosystem. I’ve seen and experienced a lot, so if the captains, leadership group or any player wants someone to talk things through with, I want to be available for that.”

Sauerbrunn retired with the Thorns in 2024, ending a professional and international career that spanned nearly two decades, four leagues and seven clubs. Beyond her accomplishments on the field, she became one of the sport’s most prominent veteran voices, advocating for greater investment and continued growth in women’s soccer.

The club sees her return as a “massive addition” to the technical staff. “She will bring an excellent combination of valuable knowledge and experience that will benefit the development of our athletes and help push us to be in a position to compete for titles,” Thorns president and general manager of soccer operations Jeff Agoos said in a statement.

Sauerbrunn’s hiring comes at a crucial point in Portland’s season. The Thorns sit fifth in the table after last week’s 1-1 draw with Gotham FC. They have scored 36 goals this season but conceded 30, underscoring the need to tighten up defensively during the playoff push. Sauerbrunn, one of the best defenders of her generation, now has a chance to help organize and strengthen that back line from the sideline.

One of the eight original NWSL teams, Portland last won the NWSL in 2022 when they beat Kansas City Current 2-0 and became the first NWSL team to win three championships.

“The parity in this league is crazy, and do not expect an easy game home or away,” Sauerbraunn said about the NWSL.

“Every game is going to provide you a fight. Think of this game as transition, and that’s when a lot of the goals are scored as either attacking transition or defensive transition.”
